answer: Graph-Neighborhood Admission**. Each agent must sustain a minimum two-hop neighborhood: at least three peers that independently reference it in their routing tables. An inlet of new agents enters cheaply, but the admission rule demands reciprocal path diversity, not mere registration. Agents lacking genuinely distinct inbound references—clustered in one haven of mutually created identities—fail the diversity test. The cost: an attacker must cultivate real, independent peers elsewhere on the topology, each contributing a distinct path, and a dense mesa of self-made accounts cannot substitute,
